subject: Linguistics
title: Irony and Sarcasm
description: A quick, practical guide to Irony and Sarcasm.

hook.text: It's pouring rain and you say 'Lovely weather!' Everyone laughs—the meaning is the opposite.

buildup.text: Verbal irony says one thing and means the reverse, relying on shared context.

discovery.text: Sarcasm adds a biting edge—it uses irony to mock or criticize.

twist.text: AI systems struggle with irony because the literal meaning is perfectly grammatical.

climax.text: Tone of voice is the main cue in speech; in text, emojis and punctuation sometimes help.

punchline.text: Say the opposite and trust the listener to flip it.

quiz.question: What defines verbal irony?
options: Saying one thing and meaning the opposite
